editorial:
Imagine living in a tiny Australian town where the biggest crime is a parking ticket. That is exactly how Gary spends his days until things get weird. He is a bored cop who spends most of his time crushing on a local reporter who wants to move to the big city. The vibe is super laid-back until a killer starts popping up and chopping off heads. The twist is that the killer is obsessed with the Village People, targeting people who look like the band members. It is a strange mix of a murder mystery and a goofy comedy that keeps you guessing who the next victim will be.

You will probably love the chemistry between the clueless Gary and the flashy city detective, Tony Charles, who thinks he is in a fancy cop show. The pacing is quick and the jokes land well, though some of the gore might be a bit much if you are squeamish. If you enjoy dark humor and quirky plots, you should definitely give this a shot. Since it is an older flick, you might want to hunt down the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to get the best picture, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: The big reveal shows that the killer is actually the town's local doctor. He wanted to complete his collection of Village People themed murders and saved the cop for last. After a tense showdown, Gary manages to outsmart the doctor and stop the killing spree. The movie ends with Gary finally getting some respect in town and a closer relationship with Julia, proving that life in a small town can actually be exciting.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark comedies and strange murder mysteries.
